extracted.intended_audience: public information officers (PIOs), emergency management communicators, and prospective PIO trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of a Public Information Officer (PIO) training program that defines core principles, skill areas, and a progressive course sequence (awareness → advanced → executive) to prepare PIOs for non-emergency preparedness and emergency response communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Right Message, to the Right People, at the Right Time
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Disaster & Emergency Management University (NDEMU) PIO training program is designed to provide PIOs with the essential knowledge, skills, and abilities to support proper decision-making by delivering the right message, to the right people, at the right time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the program's core principle: public information must enable effective communications with various target audiences and thereby support decision-making that helps save lives and protect property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential knowledge, skills, and abilities (gathering/verifying/coordinating/disseminating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public information entails the processes and systems that enable effective communications with various target audiences. The NDEMU training program provides PIOs with the opportunity to learn and practice the tasks of gathering, verifying, coordinating, and disseminating public information at all levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should develop practical competence in each task (information collection, fact-checking, coordination across agencies/stakeholders, and timely dissemination) so PIOs can support proper decision-making during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: 95/5 Concept (non-emergency vs emergency work balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 95/5 concept directly correlates to the non-emergency and emergency ratio of PIO activities: about 95% of PIO work is completed in non-emergency times, while typically about 5% is directly related to incident response or recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize investment in preparedness, relationship-building, planning, and routine communications (the 95%) because these activities significantly affect success during the 5% emergency response window. The program focuses on both non-emergency and emergency components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole community strategic communications planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses in the PIO program thematically focus on the 95/5 concept and whole community strategic communications planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIOs should be trained to design and implement strategic communications that consider the whole community (multiple audiences, partners, and access/functional needs), ensuring messages reach and are actionable for diverse populations before, during, and after emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive course sequence (awareness → advanced → master)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO program series moves progressively through public information awareness & basics to advanced PIO concepts, and culminates in a master public information officer course series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should be scaffolded so learners acquire foundational knowledge first, then advance to complex strategic functions and applied exercises, culminating in mastery-level competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information Awareness and Basics
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlying concepts, and the basic skills needed for full or part time PIOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introductory-level instruction should cover core concepts and basic operational skills necessary for entry-level or collateral-duty PIOs (e.g., basic message development, audience identification, channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic PIO
rubrics_metrics.description: A course-level element identifying foundational PIO training (Basic PIO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic PIO coursework represents essential, operational skills and knowledge for PIOs; content should align with the awareness/basics level and prepare learners for advanced coursework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Public Information Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced PIO concepts and skills for more experienced practitioners (Advanced Public Information Officer / Advanced PIO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced courses should teach higher-level strategic communications, coordination across jurisdictions, complex message development, and incident-specific public information leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Advanced Public Information Skills in a Multi-Day Functional Exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: A course/exercise element to apply advanced public information skills in a multi-day functional exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include realistic, multi-day functional exercises to practice coordination, message execution, and decision-making under simulated incident conditions; exercises validate training and readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Public Information Officer Program (expanded role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Public Information Officer Program — Expanded Role in Delivering Strategic Public Information and Warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive-level training focuses on strategic leadership, policy-level communications, and system-level responsibilities for delivering public information and warning; prepares PIOs for executive/leadership roles in communications during large or complex incidents.
